arxiv-2209-11066.description: Abstract In this paper, we report on the detection of RRab stars with quasi-identical-shape light curves but period differences as large as 0.05 − 0.21 0.05-0.21 d using the Galactic bulge data of the OGLE-IV survey. We have examined stars with shorter periods than the Oosterhoff I ridge of the bulge.

arxiv-2301-03958.title: Rigidity results for the p p -Laplacian Poisson problem with Robin boundary conditions
arxiv-2301-03958.creator: Alba Lia Masiello*, Gloria Paoli
arxiv-2301-03958.description: Abstract Let Ω ⊂ ℝ n \Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^{n} be an open, bounded and Lipschitz set. We consider the Poisson problem for the p − p- Laplace operator associated to Ω \Omega with Robin boundary conditions. In this setting, we study the equality case in the Talenti-type comparison stated in [ 6 ] .

arxiv-2405-07166.title: Resource Efficient Perception for Vision Systems
arxiv-2405-07166.creator: A V Subramanyam, Niyati Singal, Vinay K Verma
arxiv-2405-07166.description: Abstract Despite the rapid advancement in the field of image recognition, the processing of high-resolution imagery remains a computational challenge. However, this processing is pivotal for extracting detailed object insights in areas ranging from autonomous vehicle navigation to medical imaging analyses.

arxiv-2408-02735.title: Quantum information scrambling in adiabatically-driven critical systems
arxiv-2408-02735.creator: Ricardo Puebla, Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz
arxiv-2408-02735.description: Abstract Quantum information scrambling refers to the spread of the initially stored information over many degrees of freedom of a quantum many-body system. Information scrambling is intimately linked to the thermalization of isolated quantum many-body systems, and has been typically studied in a sudden quench scenario.

arxiv-2409-04181.title: Combining LLMs and Knowledge Graphs to Reduce Hallucinations in Biomedical Question Answering
arxiv-2409-04181.creator: Larissa Pusch, Tim OF Conrad
arxiv-2409-04181.description: Abstract Advancements in natural language processing (NLP), particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), have greatly improved how we access knowledge. However, in critical domains like biomedicine, challenges like hallucinations - where language models generate information not grounded in data - can lead to dangerous misinformation.

arxiv-2503-10378.title: 3D non-LTE Ca II line formation in metal-poor FGK stars
arxiv-2503-10378.creator: C. Lagae, A. M. Amarsi, K. Lind
arxiv-2503-10378.description: Abstract Context. The Ca II near-ultraviolet resonance doublet (H & \& K) and the near-infrared triplet (CaT) are among the strongest features in stellar spectra of FGK-type stars. These spectral lines remain prominent down to extremely low metallicities and are thus useful for providing stellar parameters via ionisation balance, for Galactic chemical evolution, and as radial velocity diagnostics.

arxiv-2504-02583.title: Ramírez’s problems and fibers on well approximable set of systems of affine forms
arxiv-2504-02583.creator: Bing Li, Bo Wang
arxiv-2504-02583.description: Abstract Abstract. We show that badly approximable matrices are exactly those that, for any inhomogeneous parameter, can not be inhomogeneous approximated at every monotone divergent rate, which generalizes Ramírez’s result (2018). We also establish some metrical results of the fibers on well approximable set of systems of affine forms, which gives answer to two of Ramírez’s problems (2018).

arxiv-2512-20124.title: A Certified Goal-Oriented A Posteriori Defeaturing Error Estimator for Elliptic PDEs
arxiv-2512-20124.creator: Philipp Weder 1,† and Annalisa Buffa 1,∗
arxiv-2512-20124.description: Abstract Defeaturing, the process of simplifying computational geometries, is a critical step in industrial simulation pipelines for reducing computational cost. Rigorous a posteriori estimators exist for the global energy-norm error introduced by geometry simplifications. However, practitioners are usually more concerned with the accuracy of specific quantities of interest (QoIs) in the solution.

arxiv-2602-09613.title: Tracking Finite-Time Lyapunov Exponents to Robustify Neural ODEs
arxiv-2602-09613.creator: Christian Kuehn, Tobias Wöhrer
arxiv-2602-09613.description: Abstract We investigate finite-time Lyapunov exponents (FTLEs), a measure for exponential separation of input perturbations, of deep neural networks within the framework of continuous-depth neural ODEs. We demonstrate that FTLEs are powerful organizers for input-output dynamics, allowing for better interpretability and the comparison of distinct model architectures.

pmc-11145945.creator: Niamh Murtagh, Rachael Frost
pmc-11145945.description: Highlights•Private urban gardens, especially front gardens, offer valuable eco-system services.•Understanding motivations for front gardening can help to maintain vegetation levels.•We conducted factor and regression analyses on data from a large UK survey (n = 1,000)•Enjoyment and benefit were the strongest motivations for time spent front gardening.•Motivations for beauty and functionality were also influential.

pmc-11595409.title: The Role of Digital Rectal Examination for Early Detection of Significant Prostate Cancer in the Era of Magnetic Resonance Imaging
pmc-11595409.creator: Juan Morote, Nahuel Paesano, Natàlia Picola, Jesús Muñoz-Rodriguez, Xavier Ruiz-Plazas, Marta V Muñoz-Rivero, Ana Celma, Gemma García-de Manuel, Berta Miró, José M Abascal, Pol Servian, Olga Méndez, Enrique Trilla, Paula Oliveira, Ana Faustino
pmc-11595409.description: The role of digital rectal examination (DRE) in the early detection of significant prostate cancer (PCa) is being questioned in the era of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, some men with suspected PCa may still be identified solely through DRE, even with low serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels.

pmc-12442144.title: Hospital-wide surveillance of central line-associated bloodstream infections in a tertiary hospital in South Korea
pmc-12442144.creator: Da-Mi Kim, Ji-Young Lee, Dong-Gun Lee
pmc-12442144.description: Objectives: Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections (CLABSIs) are associated with prolonged hospitalization, increased healthcare costs. It is important to reduce CLABSI rates through interventions. This study investigated the current status of CLABSI rates among hospitalized patients to gather foundational data for implementing CLABSI intervention measures.

pmc-12678990.title: Effects of endoscopic mucosal resection and argon plasma coagulation on postoperative recovery and complications in elderly colon polyp patients
pmc-12678990.creator: Hong-Tao Li, Feng Liu, Peng-Fei Mei, Xia Lei, Shen-Ying Liu
pmc-12678990.description: BACKGROUNDColon polyps represent a significant clinical challenge in elderly patients. While endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) and argon plasma coagulation (APC) are widely used, their comparative effectiveness in elderly populations remains unclear, particularly regarding postoperative recovery and complication profiles.AIMTo compare the postoperative recovery, complications and efficacy of EMR and APC in elderly patients with colonic polyps.

pmc-13013598.title: Model predictive game control for personalized and targeted interactive assistance
pmc-13013598.creator: Abdelwaheb Hafs, Anaïs Farr, Dorian Verdel, Olivier Bruneau, Etienne Burdet, Bastien Berret
pmc-13013598.description: Contact robots are increasingly used to assist humans in physical training and manufacturing tasks. However, their effectiveness is currently limited as control methods focus on system performance without considering the upcoming human user’s control. Here, we present a differential game-based controller for contact robots ensuring optimal interaction by predicting human motor control over their finite planning horizon.

pmc-13198134.title: When Ebstein Meets Fallot
pmc-13198134.creator: Jules Ader, Charlène Bredy, Jean-Luc Pasquié
pmc-13198134.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Case SummaryA 14-year-old boy was admitted after resuscitated ventricular fibrillation. He had tetralogy of Fallot associated with Ebstein's anomaly, surgically repaired at age 7 without tricuspid intervention. His ECG demonstrates overlapping features of both conditions: high-amplitude right bundle branch block and right ventricular hypertrophy consistent with repaired tetralogy of Fallot, along with broad “Himalayan” P waves, first-degree atrioventricular block, and fragmented QRS complexes reflecting Ebstein-related conduction abnormalities.

pmc-13247971.title: Association between myocardial involvement and subclinical left ventricular dysfunction in patients with systemic sclerosis: a cardiac magnetic resonance study
pmc-13247971.creator: Yafeng Peng, Huilin He, Xinyu Tong, Bowei Liu, Wushi Shao, Dong Xu, Xihai Zhao, Haiyan Ding, Jinzhi Lai, Zuo-Xiang He
pmc-13247971.description: BackgroundMyocardial involvement frequently occurs in patients with systemic sclerosis (SSc), leading to myocardial tissue changes and subclinical ventricular dysfunction. This form of primary cardiac involvement is one of the major determinants of mortality in SSc and may eventually progress to overt heart failure.

pmc-13637406.title: P2X4 receptor limits adverse cardiac remodeling following ischemia–reperfusion through regulation of autophagy in cardiac fibroblasts
pmc-13637406.creator: Ana Valeria Vinhais da Silva, Juliette Strella, Simon Chesseron, Arthur Aupart, Audrey Heraud-Meley, Elodie Miquelestorena-Standley, Marc Ohresser, Ludovica Congiu, Eric Boué-Grabot, Thierry Bourguignon, Sébastien Roger, Stephanie Chadet, Fabrice Ivanes
pmc-13637406.description: BackgroundPathological ventricular remodeling is an adverse tissue response following acute myocardial infarction (AMI), characterized by an exaggerated fibrosis leading to tissue disorganization and chronic heart failure. Cardiac fibroblasts have a prominent role in the healing process, but also in the fibrosis development, through their differentiation into myofibroblasts, which produce the extracellular matrix, in response to ischemia–reperfusion.
